How blindfold play works: In {n} Paul Morphy watched an opera in Paris, and between the acts he played two noblemen together. They played slowly and passively, moving the same pieces again and again. Morphy did the opposite: every move brought a new piece into play. When their king was still in the centre, he sacrificed a knight, then a rook, then his queen. With only a bishop and a rook left, he gave checkmate. Lesson: fast development beats extra material.
Blindfold khel kaise chalta hai: {n} mein Paul Morphy Paris mein opera dekh rahe the, aur beech mein unhone do raeeson ke saath ek saath khela. Wo dheere aur dabe hue khele, baar baar wahi pieces chalate rahe. Morphy ne ulta kiya: har chaal ek naya piece khel mein laayi. Jab unka king abhi bhi centre mein tha, unhone knight, phir rook, phir apni queen qurbaan ki. Sirf ek bishop aur rook bache the, aur unhone checkmate de diya. Seekh: tez development extra material se behtar hai.

How blindfold play works: In {n}, {n}-year-old Bobby Fischer played a strong master, Donald Byrne. On move {n} Fischer let his queen be taken. In return he got a rook, two bishops and a pawn, and his pieces worked like a team. A "windmill" of knight checks won even more, and he finished with mate. It was called "The Game of the Century". Lesson: count the whole position, not just the queen.

Ise "The Game of the Century" kaha gaya. Seekh: sirf queen nahi, poori position gino.
